title: Blackstone’s Jas Khaira says fears over AI-buildout debt are overblown
slides: Is Blackstone's AI debt bet safe?
Jas Khaira dismisses fears over buildout borrowing
But debt structures hide risks investors rarely see
Watch covenant terms in AI infrastructure deals
Ask what happens if AI demand stalls
thread_text:
1. The $1 trillion question

Blackstone is piling into AI infrastructure debt. Jas Khaira, the firm's global head of structured finance, insists the buildout borrowing is safe. But the real risk hides in the fine print.

2. Not all debt is equal

Structured deals let borrowers stack layers of leverage behind a single asset. Each layer adds a new set of investors with different priorities — and different claims on cash flow when things go wrong.

3. Covenants are the tripwire

Legal terms buried in hundreds of pages decide who gets paid first and who absorbs losses. They also dictate when lenders can force a restructuring — often before a project is even finished.

4. When demand stalls

AI infrastructure is built on projections of explosive growth. If demand plateaus or delays, covenant breaches can trigger forced sales at fire-sale prices. Khaira's optimism assumes the music never stops.

5. Check your own exposure

If you own Blackstone funds or AI-linked bonds, pull the offering documents today. Ask one question: what happens if AI demand misses projections by 20%? If you can't answer it, you're flying blind.
